question: Why did the p95 latency go up on 26 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: The deployment of the search v3.1 to eu-west increased request volume and led to higher p95 latency.
why_chain: The deployment of search v3.1 to eu-west caused a surge in request volume.
The surge in request volume overwhelmed the autoscaler, leading to scaling out and increased latency.
The increased latency resulted in the observed p95 latency rise.

contributing_factors.description: The change in the checkout feature flag led to a flash sale campaign, increasing request volume.
why_chain: The change in the checkout feature flag triggered the flash sale campaign.
The flash sale campaign increased request volume, which in turn caused the p95 latency rise.
The increased request volume overwhelmed the system, leading to higher latency.

contributing_factors.description: The rise in request volume due to the flash sale campaign caused the autoscaler to scale out, leading to higher p95 latency.
why_chain: The flash sale campaign increased request volume.
The increased request volume caused the autoscaler to scale out.
The scaling out led to higher p95 latency.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The autoscaler scaling out was due to a bug in the autoscaler itself.
ruled_out.reason: There is no evidence that the autoscaler scaling out was due to a bug. The evidence points to the flash sale campaign as the cause.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in p95 latency was due to a configuration issue in the search service.
ruled_out.reason: The deployment of search v3.1 was routine and did not indicate a configuration issue. The evidence points to the flash sale campaign as the cause.

evidence.summary: P95 latency for region eu-west rose from 137 ms to 224 ms (+64%), with a change point at 2026-03-26T13:45:00Z.
The change is concentrated in region eu-west: 4 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.02).
At the same time, request volume for region eu-west rose (2118 per 5 min before, 7734 per 5 min after, +265%).
At the same time, error rate for region eu-west rose (0.48% before, 0.97% after, +102%).
Changed checkout feature flag new_ui_flow to 50% in eu-west (checkout, eu-west; 3 min before the change; record R016)
Marketing: flash sale campaign goes live in eu-west at 13:45 UTC (eu-west; 220 min before the change; record R014)
Request volume 3x normal in eu-west (eu-west; 12 min after the change; record R017)
Deployed search v3.1 to eu-west (routine release) (search, eu-west; 136 min before the change; record R015)
autoscaler: scaling out, 4 new instances requested (eu-west; 20 min after the change; record R018)

reasons: ✗ The closest change event is 136 min before the change, too far to be convincing.
✓ 2 log/alert record(s) after the change agree with the numbers.
✗ Request volume also rose, so a traffic explanation is still open.
✗ 2 other change event(s) fit about as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.
missing_data: Change records from the hour before the change
Details to tell the competing changes apart (e.g. a rollback test)

actions.action: Roll back the search v3.1 deployment to eu-west.
Monitor the autoscaler and ensure it is configured correctly to avoid scaling out during normal operations.
Review and optimize the autoscaler configuration to handle sudden spikes in request volume more gracefully.
